name: Bloc Projects
known: Director is Dr Yet Chor Sunshine Wong.
The board of trustees is co-chaired by Adrian Friedli and Jeanine Griffin (Bloc Projects website).

name: Site Gallery
known: It moved to 1 Brown Street in 1988 under director Matthew Conduit (Wikipedia).
Sharna Jackson has been artistic director since July 2018 (Wikipedia).
Judith Harry is Chief Executive (accounts).

name: John Hansard Gallery
known: Directors: Leo Stable (1979 to 1980), Barry Barker (1980 to 1987), Professor Stephen Foster (1987 to 2017) and Woodrow Kernohan (2017 to the present) (gallery about page).

name: Coaxial Arts Foundation
known: Founded by Eva Aguila.

Hyperallergic (2024) says the residency launched in 2016 with inaugural residents JJ Stratford and Suzy Poling, and that residents work without curator oversight and receive studio space and access to video and sound equipment.

name: Human Resources LA (HRLA)
known: Programme: exhibitions, performances, music and sound events, readings and screenings, organised by a content programming committee rather than a single curator (Wikipedia).
The Mike Kelley Foundation grants page lists the group exhibition "There in Green California", curated by Gelare Khoshgozaran, for April 2024.
The executive director is John Burdle.

name: LACE (Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions)
known: Joy Silverman became the first executive director in 1982 and Sarah Russin is the current executive director (Wikipedia).
Andy Warhol Foundation: $80,000 over two years from 2015 for the Emerging Curators series, the Project Room and a summer residency (LACE, 30 July 2015).
Teiger Foundation: a 2025 grant for three years of programming led by Selene Preciado, Curator and Director of Programming (LACE; amount not stated).

name: REDCAT (Roy and Edna Disney/CalArts Theater)
known: João Ribas was hired in 2019 as the first CalArts Vice President for Cultural Partnerships and Executive Director of REDCAT.
Mark Murphy was the first executive director of REDCAT (Wikipedia).
A REDCAT Council, chaired by Diane Levine, is listed on the site (REDCAT website).

name: American Folk Art Museum
known: Deborah Davenport and Stewart Stender gave $3 million to establish a curator position (stated by the space, November 2025 letter; the gift year is not given).
Director and CEO Jason T.

name: Apexart
known: The tax filing is under the name Apex Art Curatorial Program Inc, a 501(c)(3) exempt since April 1998, with Rand listed as president and executive director (ProPublica).

Programmes: the NYC Open Call and International Open Call, an Invited Curator series, an Unsolicited Proposal Program, a Franchise Program that stages shows outside New York, a one-month fellowship abroad, and publications (Wikipedia; apexart website; e-flux).

Finances (ProPublica, Apex Art Curatorial Program Inc): 2025 revenue $668,067, expenses $694,684, contributions $663,949, net assets $102,706; 2024 revenue $712,957, expenses $764,291; 2023 revenue $693,524, expenses $657,819; 2022 revenue $720,160.
ProPublica lists Steven Rand as president and executive director and Rosemary O'Neill as treasurer.
Democratic blind-curatorial open calls, international idea-driven exhibitions, essays, public fellowship

name: Brooklyn Academy of Music (BAM)
known: Leadership: Tamara McCaw is president and Amy Cassello artistic director (BAM site).

name: CUE Art Foundation
known: Hsu, with painter Gregory Amenoff as co-founder and titular head.
Hsu (Chairman), Theodore S.
Executive Director Jinny Khanduja received $110,000 in reported compensation in 2024 (ProPublica).

name: Flux Factory
known: Nat Roe was executive director in 2021 (The Art Newspaper, Hyperallergic).

name: New Museum of Contemporary Art
known: Founded in 1977 by curator Marcia Tucker, who led it until 1999.
Massimiliano Gioni was named director in July 2026 (Wikipedia).
Mellon Foundation: 1,500,000 dollars on 8 December 2022 for 36 months to support NEW INC's new director, Salome Asega (Mellon Foundation).

name: Printed Matter, Inc.
known: Ingrid Sischy was the first director in 1976.
AA Bronson was executive director from 2004 to 2010 and started the New York Art Book Fair in 2006 (Wikipedia).

Phil Aarons: W Magazine describes him as a real estate developer, co-founder of Millennium Partners and the board's president in 2014; he sits on the MoMA PS1 board, and the 2023 fair site thanks him and Shelley Fox Aarons by name.
Board chair Philip Aarons co-founded luxury developer Millennium Partners and was founding chair of Friends of the High Line.
